stem: A patient asks to receive only part of a new oxymorphone prescription today and return for the balance. Which limit must be documented?

choices.text: Treat it as a patient-requested Schedule II partial fill and dispense any lawful remainder within the applicable 30-day window.
Use the out-of-state prescription rule when its schedule, age, and verification conditions have not been checked.
Process another refill because an authorization written by the prescriber overrides schedule limits.
Treat the request as an insufficient-stock partial fill and use the 72-hour remainder rule.
Handle the drug or transaction as ordinary Massachusetts Schedule VI activity.

explanation.core_reasoning: A Schedule II prescription may be partially filled at the patient or prescriber request when state law permits, with the remaining portion dispensed no later than 30 days after the prescription was written unless a shorter applicable limit controls. oxymorphone (Opana) is used for pain severe enough to require an opioid when alternatives are inadequate. It is federal Schedule II and Massachusetts Schedule II; its legal consequence in this scenario follows the cited schedule-specific rule.
